title: Electron speed calculation
description: Essential: Student must compute the final electron speed using energy conservation or work-energy theorem, obtaining approximately 1.0×10⁸ m/s.

title: Photon count per second
description: Essential: Student must calculate the number of X-ray photons per second from the given current, obtaining approximately 6.25×10¹⁶.

title: Energy conversion reasoning
description: Important: Student should explicitly state that the electron's kinetic energy equals the work done by the electric field (eU) and is converted to X-ray photon energy.

title: Current-photon relationship
description: Important: Student must recognize that photon emission rate equals electron arrival rate, and correctly relate current to number of electrons per second.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: Student demonstrates unit analysis for both calculations, confirming final units are m/s and photons/second.

title: Relativistic oversight
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly applies relativistic formulas for electron speed (v≈0.33c) when non-relativistic treatment is adequate here.

title: Current conversion error
description: Pitfall: Student fails to convert mA to A or misplaces powers of ten in the photon count calculation.
